properties.name: A typed edge helper handed a node of the wrong type reports the node as MISSING, then spends a paragraph on a parallel-batch race that did not happen — while create_edge draws the same edge without complaint
properties.statement: FLO2 F11, twice in one session (`depends_on` on two Decisions, `operates_in` on a Component), and REPRODUCED on the current binary 0.65.0 on 2026-09-19: `depends_on {from_id: dec:a, to_id: dec:b}` against a scratch design holding both answers `Node not found: Component dec:a`, followed by the parallel-batch paragraph. `create_edge {edge_type: DEPENDS_ON, from_id: dec:a, to_id: dec:b}` on the SAME pair, the same second, succeeds — DEPENDS_ON between two Decisions is a legal edge. So the helper reports as ABSENT a node that exists, names a type the caller never mentioned, and offers a cause (an unordered batch) that was not what happened. The reporter nearly re-created a node that was already there. ⭐ AND THE CONTRAST IS THE USEFUL PART, in their words: falling back to the generic tool produced an excellent refusal — 'Invalid edge: OPERATES_IN cannot connect Component to Environment' plus every edge type that WOULD accept the pair — which taught them the model and stopped them forcing a wrong edge. THE GENERIC TOOL GIVES A BETTER ERROR THAN THE TYPED HELPER IT IS A FALLBACK FOR, which is backwards from what a caller expects, and this is the second entry in that file to say so.
